title: Generic Stack
instructions:
Write a generic class called `Stack<T>` that works like a stack of plates -- the last item you add is the first one you remove.

Your class needs:
1. A `push(item: T)` method that adds an item to the top of the stack.
2. A `pop(): T` method that removes and returns the top item. If the stack is empty, throw an `IllegalStateException` with the message `"Stack is empty"`.
3. An `isEmpty(): Boolean` method that returns `true` if the stack has no items.

Use a `MutableList<T>` inside the class to store the items.
hint: Create a private `val items = mutableListOf<T>()` inside the class. For `push`, use `items.add(item)`. For `pop`, check if empty first, then use `items.removeAt(items.size - 1)`. For `isEmpty`, return `items.isEmpty()`.
